# STX Downloader: full reference

> An open-source Windows app, MIT licensed, published by Strategia-X (Rocky Elsalaymeh). It saves media you are allowed to keep, from YouTube and from web pages, tells you what the audio really is, and plays your whole collection with VLC's engine. It looks like a piece of solid-state rack gear.

Version 1.2.0, released 2026-11-15. Project page: https://git-rocky-stack.github.io/STX-Downloader/ . Source: https://github.com/Git-Rocky-Stack/STX-Downloader . Support: support@strategia-x.com

Each feature below is described in the project README, which names the code that does it by file and member: https://github.com/Git-Rocky-Stack/STX-Downloader#what-it-does

## Scope

- DRM is out of scope. STX doesn't save or play DRM-protected media. When it sees DRM, it says so and stops.
- Users are responsible for following each site's terms and the law where they live.

## Requirements and install

- Windows 10 version 2004 or later, x64.
- About 400 MB of disk for the app, and about 430 MB for its tools.
- No administrator prompt: the setup installs for the user's account only, and uninstalls from Windows Settings. Saved media is never removed.
- .NET and the Windows App SDK ship inside the app; there is no runtime to install first.
- The setup also installs yt-dlp, FFmpeg and Deno, each checked against its publisher's checksum, so the first launch downloads nothing and works offline.
- The setup and the app's own files are signed through Azure Artifact Signing. Windows shows the publisher as Sharif Elsalaymeh.
- Downloads for 1.2.0: STXDownloader-1.2.0-setup.exe (254 MB, SHA-256 1E067230272C7223E1A9430E0B9BFF8E3ADF8C8666477CB2323C2592E7590363) and STXDownloader-1.2.0-win-x64.zip (171 MB, the app alone, SHA-256 FEAF84A7A1CE1168F31DB827D637F42745886DB1AFF17DA30DFA86BAB53308F1), at https://github.com/Git-Rocky-Stack/STX-Downloader/releases/tag/v1.2.0
- Capturing from pages needs the Chrome or Edge extension, loaded unpacked from the extension folder inside the install folder.

## Saving

- Paste a link and yt-dlp handles it, single items and playlists. A playlist asks first: add its items, just the video the link names, or cancel. Private and unavailable items are skipped, and counted.
- Video isn't re-encoded by default. It keeps the original streams, in MP4 when they fit and MKV when they don't.
- A name already taken by another video never replaces it; the new file gets its id added.
- A new file with the same bytes as one already saved is removed, and the Library points at the first copy.
- CAR USB, PHONE and ARCHIVE convert a saved file when asked.
- A captured job whose link expired waits for a new capture from its page, and resumes from it.

## Capturing from a page

- A Chrome and Edge extension lists the page's HLS, DASH and direct media, collapses renditions, and hands over YouTube embeds by ID.
- If the page uses DRM, its streams get no Save button.
- Hand-off uses Chrome native messaging and a named pipe only the user's Windows account can open. No network port is opened.

## Secrets

- Stream tokens, cookies and headers stay in memory and reach yt-dlp through a temp file only the user can read, deleted when the job ends.
- They are scrubbed from the log the user can copy.

## Source Truth

- Measures the saved file's audio rather than repeating what the site claims, and shows the spectrum, the roll-off, loudness and true peak.
- Gives a plain verdict for each output format, and never says re-encoding improved anything.

## Library

- Holds what the user has saved, files opened with STX, and the media in the Videos and Music folders, which are watched from the first launch.
- Removing a row or a watched folder never removes a file from disk.
- The database counts, pages and searches the rows: 50,000 rows cost no more memory than an empty Library.

## Playing

- Uses the official VLC 3.0.24 engine for Windows, pinned by sha256, with the parts that would open network ports or run site scripts left out.
- Plays 120 file types, each proven by a file in the test corpus, and can register as the default player for the user's account.
- Plays unencrypted DVD and Blu-ray. Encrypted discs are refused by STX before VLC's engine sees them.
- Plays streams and internet radio, including .pls and .m3u playlists. UDP and RTP are refused because they would need a listening port.
- BIT-PERFECT, off by default, sends lossless music to the sound device at the file's own rate and depth, holding the device exclusively.
- ENHANCE offers OFF, SHARPEN or UPSCALE for the picture on screen. UPSCALE is GPU super resolution, offered only on NVIDIA RTX with a 530 or later driver, and Intel Arc and Xe.
- Dirac and VC-2 video are refused, because VLC 3.0.24's engine crashes on them.
- Parity with VLC is tested: a corpus of 178 files covers 89 of the 91 formats and codecs on VideoLAN's list for 3.0.24, plus HEVC Main10, HDR10, AV1 and VP9.

## Shrink

- SHRINK makes a smaller copy beside the selected file: AV1 or HEVC video with Opus sound, or Opus for sound alone. SHRINK FOLDER does the same for a whole folder.
- A copy is kept only after it decodes from start to end without errors, has the original's picture and sound, and lasts as long.
- The original is only ever read. STX never deletes it.

## The console

- Black anodized by default, brushed aluminum as light mode. Text meets WCAG AA contrast on both.
- Per-monitor DPI aware.
- A user guide that opens on the first launch, and seven tutorials that walk a spotlight over the live console.

## Releases

- 1.2.0 (2026-11-15): 120 file types up from 51, tutorials on the live console, a rebuilt user guide, CLEAR and CLEAR DONE for the Queue, REMOVE and CLEAR MISSING for the Library, new meters.
- 1.1.0 (2026-11-09): a media player on VLC's engine, STX as the default player, discs and streams, bit-perfect sound, ENHANCE, and Shrink.
- 1.0.0 (2026-11-01): the first release.
